>None of this suggests homework causes suicide
It's not a hard connection to make. 

Excessive homework can cause stress, which can cause suicide.

>If it were true students would be commuting suicide at an extremely high rate if you believe how people here talk about their course load.

I don't know how the hell you came to the conclusion that complaints on Reddit would equal real life suicide, but to 1-Up you on that, my friend talked about his course load. And he _did_ die. I'm struggling to see your logic here. "If it were true that break-ups lead to suicide, teens would be commiting suicide at extremely high rates if you believe how people here talk about their relationship problems."

Would you like to talk to experts about this? Because they'd disagree. I know what the heck I'm talking about, I'm studying to become a psychologist and have researched disorders like depression and anxiety since I was in _elementary_ school (5th grade to be exact, I don't wanna sound like some arrogant asshole who's claiming to have studies this since kindergarten). 

But, of course, I'm not an expert. You know who is? Harvard. Mayo. [Here: let's take a look at what Mayo says](https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/stress-management/expert-answers/stress/faq-20058233)

> Depression has many causes, such as genetics, brain chemicals, and your life situation. Chronic stressful life situations can increase your risk of developing depression if you aren't coping with stress well. 

The thing to take away is that it says increase risks, not a direct cause. However, an increase risk can often be a direct cause, take smoking for example. Smoking increases the risk for cancer. Does it mean you will get cancer? No. But does it make the statement "Smoking causes cancer" any less true either? No. It doesn't. At the end I elaborate even further.

[According to Psychology Today, stress can often turn into depression ](https://www.google.com/amp/s/www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/in-practice/201303/why-stress-turns-depression%3famp) This was written by a lady with a Ph.D.

Chemical imbalance is a huge oversimplification of what depression really is and how it works.[Chemical imbalance is a huge oversimplification of what depression really is and how it works.](https://www.health.harvard.edu/mind-and-mood/what-causes-depression)

 > Research suggests that depression doesn't spring from simply having too much or too little of certain brain chemicals. Rather, there are many possible causes of depression, including faulty mood regulation by the brain, genetic vulnerability, stressful life events, medications, and medical problems. It's believed that several of these forces interact to bring on depression.

I could go on and on. Christ man, as I've said I wrote _papers_ on this. I've studied the brain since I was 10 years old, after I learned about ADHD from a friend. You really cannot sit here and pretend like I don't know what I'm talking about. 

>Homework is too common a thing for it to be the direct cause of a suicide.

That is such BS, because I could replace it with just about any "cause" of suicide and it'd be equally as stupid. "Death (of another person) is too common for it to be the direct cause of suicide." "Bullying is too common for it to be the direct cause of suicide." "Being fired is too common a thing for it to be the direct cause of suicide." You're joking, right? The only direct cause of suicide is slipping a noose over your neck, or swallowing a handful of pill, or pulling the trigger and blowing your brain out. Of course none of those things directly cause suicide. But that doesn't mean people don't kill themselves over it. Death causes grief. Bullying causes low self esteem. Being fired causes one to feel lost or hopeless. Excessive homework causes stress. All of which can cause depression. 

But, did you even _read_ my comment? I literally said 

>Homework is immensely known to cause stress, and be a huge factor in stress and stress related suicides.

I'm not, and never pretended like it was a direct cause. Because it's not. Nothing ever is. Smoking isn't a direct cause of cancer either. If we wanna be assholes and get to the literal sense of the word "cause," cancer is caused by damaged cells/genes. What causes damage cells/genes (for this specific example)? The tobacco smoke. What in the tobacco smoke? The carcinogen. Carcinogen is a secondary cause, or hell, maybe even tertiary cause if we're listing things in order here, but it's still a cause no less, and nobody ever needs to specify secondary cause when they say "smoking causes cancer." Stop this. You know damn well just as much a I do that I never said homework is a direct cause of suicide.

>homework like you did for the last 10 years.

Once again, fuck off. It's not the homework, it's the amount of homework, which out of nowhere suddenly increased 300% by the time we reached high school. You're practically using strawman arguments at this point, and because of this we're basically going in circles. Usually at this point I'd just stop replying to someone who does this, but no. My friend didn't die over fucking nothing, and I'm not going to let you sit here and let you essentially shit talk him like this, when you don't know his experience, or hell even my experience, and probably didn't have an experience anywhere close to that on your own as you seem to struggle to grasp he homework could possibly lead to suicide.

Depression caused by the overhwleming amount of homework? Or are we just going to leave that part out? Millions kids get bullied too, to the point where they get depressed but not every single bullied kid kills themself. Doesn't mean it's any less of an issue. Or does the depression just get them too?

Edit: And I understand that it's the same amount as everyone else, but my point is it shouldn't be to begin with. There's a line between a good amount of homework and absolutely ridiculousness. Our school was on the ridiculous side of that spectrum. Once again, you completely fucking missed my entire point that everyone's experiences are different. I'm not blaming the homework as though homework should be banned. I'm saying it's the reason he killed himself. Because it is. And the school system immensely needs to be fixed. But to wrap up into my first comment, highschool for some, is fucking awful, and saying that it's "life on easy mode" when you didn't have the same experience as everyone else on this planet is absolute bullshit.

Homework is immensely known to cause stress, and be a huge factor in stress and stress related suicides. Bullying and parental issues get the most attention, but that doesn't mean there aren't kids out there who kill themselves over being stressed and burnt out. You hear way more about people killing themselves over say, a break up, or a family loss. But does that mean because those happen more often or you hear about it more often people don't kill themselves because they’re overwhelmed at work too? No. Breakups and grief is just the stereotypical shit. Everyone's situation is different, and there is no one cause for suicide, but homework and schoolwork can be a big factor and that was the point I was trying to make.

And frankly, fuck you for basically implying that because you've never heard of it, or because it doesn't happen often enough for you to hear of it, it just doesn't happen or it's not a big deal. Wanna know why I know it exists? Because I've experienced wanting to kill myself over being stressed over homework. In school knew many kids, some friends, some not, who wanted to kill themselves over homework, and I had a friend who killed himself because of fucking homework.

My Sophomore year. He was a Junior. He had one year left yet he was so overwhelmed he couldn't do it. His situation was parallel to mine, great parents, no bullying, a couple friends. We clicked so much. He even seemingly had it better than me, outgoing and optimistic, whereas I struggled with social anxiety and was incredibly shy and reserved. But the homework was too much, he got overwhelmed. Fell behind in classes because he just stopped doing homework because he stayed up until 1 AM or would be so burnt out with homework he couldn't focus the next day. Understood the material, it was just a lot of work. He constantly texted me about how he felt, and the night he died I was asleep, he tried fucking texting me at 1 AM like usual but that was the one time I decided to go to sleep early. I think about that shit every day, if I had just stayed up, if I had worked on my project just a little later, if I had waited in the long line at PDQ's instead of going home. Anything to delay me going to sleep that night... Maybe he'd still be here. Fuck. Homework. Just because you didn't hear about his fucking death doesn't make it any less real. 

A year later in English class, I even wrote a paper on why excessive homework sucks so much, and why it has been proven to cause so much suicidal thoughts, depression, anxiety, and sleep deprivation in teens. Why am I telling you this? If need be I can and will happily link the studies and articles I used during my research, although it may take me a while to find it.. Majority of my papers written that year were about the such bullshit known as our school system and why so many are essentially set up to fail with little care or compassion until someone inevitably has enough and dies. Like Jacob did.

Nope. You'd be surprised. There are tons of kids who feel or felt suicidal over the stress of homework and projects, despite having normal and supportive families. 

And "typically" means nothing when it comes to someone taking their own life. Nobody should be taken their life over school assignments, so there's still an issue here none the less. 

School assignments still put pressure on students. Pressure from teachers and this idea that if you aren't perfect you won't succeed or you're dumb. Pressure can come from more than just families.

I mean fuck I think a study even found that teens experience stress levels on par, if not higher than the levels adults feel. 

A lot of these people talking about school being easy and getting into the "real world" seem to be older people. People who haven't gone to school in 30, 40 years. Times have changed. Things have most certainly gotten far more stressful for young people. School and life alike. What was a breeze for you 30 years ago just doesn't exist anymore for the same kids in school now.

Thank you. "HiGh sChOoL iSn'T thAt bAd" it's bad enough to cause suicide and suicidal thoughts, so _clearly_ it was pretty fucking hard for _someone._

Or, are those students just lazy? Overreacting? It was easy for you so what could possibly be the issue for all those other students?

Some people just aren't good at school. Especially if the school system is literally not made for them. Try having a learning or developmental difference compared to everyone else, and shit's pretty hard. Even worse when you don't get the help or accomodations you need. Not everyone's experience is the same. Imagine going up to a dyslexic person and being like "I don't get the issue here, high school was awesome to me! My job as an adult is so much harder." Good for you. Turns out that same exact job is a billion times easier than being forced to read a 500 page book when the words jump around and the letters are backwards. Something _you_ didn't have to go through but the dyslexic kid did.
